input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers a per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web console.
Cluster administrators selecting a project see every workbench in the project
with its last activity, its owner, and its reserved resources
(CPU/memory/gpu reservations), so they can judge which workbenches are idle.
The report is sourced from the notebook
controller's existing activity tracking — no new tracking is built. The epic
also delivers CSV export of this report so administrators can take the data
offline for auditing and reclamation planning.

## Scope

- Console backend aggregation of per-project workbench data: last-activity
  timestamp from the notebook controller's activity tracking, workbench owner,
  and reserved resources read from the workbench (Notebook) custom resources.
- A per-project, administrator-facing report view in the web console listing
  every workbench in the project with its last activity, owner, and reserved
  resources. The strategy defines no idleness threshold for workbenches (unlike
  the configurable age for stale pipeline runs), so the report applies no
  threshold: it presents the activity data for all workbenches and the
  administrator judges idleness.
- CSV export of the idle-workbench report.
- Validation of the notebook controller as a passive data source: confirm the
  report's last-activity values match the timestamps the notebook controller
  actually tracks for the same workbenches (read-only consumption — the
  notebook controller itself is not modified).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches with differing activity levels, when
  an administrator opens the idle-workbench report for that project, then every
  workbench in the project is listed with its last activity, owner, and reserved
  resources — the report applies no idleness threshold; the administrator judges
  idleness from the displayed activity data.
- Given the notebook controller's tracked last-activity timestamps for a set of
  workbenches, when the report is generated for the same project, then the
  report's last-activity values match the controller's tracked values.
- Given the idle-workbench report, when an administrator chooses to export it,
  then a CSV file containing the report's rows and columns is produced.
- The report is delivered without code changes to the notebook controller (the
  console consumes existing activity data only).

## HLR Traceability

| HLR | Priority | Coverage |
|-----|----------|----------|
| HLR-1 — per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources) sourced from notebook controller activity tracking | P1 | Fully covered by this epic. |
| HLR-3 — administrators can export either report as CSV | P2 | Bundled: CSV export of this report is a presentation mode of the same report surface over the same data — it is not separately schedulable, so it ships with the report it exports. |

# Stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web console

## Description

This epic delivers a stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web console. Cluster
administrators selecting a project see pipeline runs that completed longer ago
than a configurable age threshold and still retain artifacts, so they can
identify runs whose accumulated storage is reclaimable. The report is sourced
from Kubeflow Pipelines' existing run completion metadata — no new metadata
capture is built. The epic also delivers CSV export of this report.

## Scope

- Console backend query of per-project pipeline run completion metadata from
  Kubeflow Pipelines: run identity, completion time, and retained-artifact
  information for completed runs.
- An administrator-configurable age threshold defining when a completed run
  counts as stale.
- A per-project, administrator-facing report view in the web console listing
  stale completed runs with their retained artifacts.
- CSV export of the stale pipeline-run report.
- Validation of Kubeflow Pipelines as a passive data source: confirm the
  report's run data matches the pipeline run metadata retained by Kubeflow
  Pipelines for the same project (read-only consumption — Kubeflow Pipelines
  itself is not modified).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project with completed pipeline runs of various ages, when an
  administrator opens the stale pipeline-run report for that project with a
  given age threshold, then exactly the completed runs older than that
  threshold are listed together with their retained artifacts.
- Given the administrator changes the staleness age threshold, when the report
  is regenerated, then the listed runs reflect the new threshold without code
  changes or redeployment.
- Given the pipeline run metadata retained by Kubeflow Pipelines for a project,
  when the report is generated for the same project, then the report's run
  entries match that retained metadata.
- Given the stale pipeline-run report, when an administrator chooses to export
  it, then a CSV file containing the report's rows and columns is produced.
- The report is delivered without code changes to Kubeflow Pipelines (the
  console consumes existing run metadata only).

## HLR Traceability

| HLR | Priority | Coverage |
|-----|----------|----------|
| HLR-2 — stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata | P1 | Fully covered by this epic. |
| HLR-3 — administrators can export either report as CSV | P2 | Bundled: CSV export of this report is a presentation mode of the same report surface over the same data — it is not separately schedulable, so it ships with the report it exports. |

# Documentation for the idle resource reports and safe reclamation

## Description

This epic delivers Red Hat documentation for the console's idle resource
reporting capability: what the idle-workbench report and the stale pipeline-run
report show, where their data comes from, how to read and export them, and —
critically — the safe steps an administrator follows to reclaim capacity from
resources the reports identify as idle or stale. It documents the reports as
implemented, which is why it runs after both report implementations.

## Scope

Content outline (topics to be authored in the RHOAI documentation set):

- **Idle resource reporting overview** — what the capability is for, who it is
  for (cluster administrators), and the per-project scope of both reports.
- **Idle-workbench report** — how to read the last-activity, owner, and
  reserved-resources columns; where the activity data comes from (notebook
  controller activity tracking); and the limits of that data.
- **Stale pipeline-run report** — how the configurable staleness age threshold
  works, what "retained artifacts" means, and where the run data comes from
  (Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata).
- **Exporting reports as CSV** — how administrators export either report.
- **Safe reclamation steps** — the documented, cautious procedure for
  reclaiming capacity from idle workbenches and stale runs (manual actions,
  what to verify first, what cannot be undone), including an explicit note
  that automated reclamation is not provided.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation explains both reports, their data sources, and their
  columns, matching the behavior of the reports as implemented in the web
  console.
- Published documentation explains how to configure the stale-run age threshold
  and how to export either report as CSV.
- Published documentation provides step-by-step safe reclamation guidance for
  idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs, including the caveat that
  reclamation is manual.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented reports by
  the console engineering team before publication.

## HLR Traceability

| HLR | Priority | Coverage |
|-----|----------|----------|
| HLR-4 — documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps | P2 | Fully covered by this epic. |

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9016 (Idle resource reporting in the web console)

## Triage

Not below threshold: although the code change is confined to one active component
(the web console), the scope spans two architecturally distinct data-source
integrations (notebook-controller activity tracking vs. Kubeflow Pipelines run
metadata) that warrant separate PR review cycles, plus a substantive
documentation work stream (HLR-4 — new doc topics, not incidental touch-ups).
Not docs-only: the web console requires code changes. Full decomposition follows.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 | Per-project idle-workbench report in the RHOAI web console | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E002 | Stale pipeline-run report in the RHOAI web console | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9016-E003 | Documentation for the idle resource reports and safe reclamation | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHAI Documentation | P2 |

## Component Mapping

| Strategy component | Canonical Jira component | Active/Passive | Handling |
|---------------------|---------------------------|----------------|----------|
| RHOAI web console | Dashboard | Active | Epics E001, E002 (all code change lives here) |
| Notebook controller | Notebooks | Passive | Data source only — validated as an acceptance criterion on E001 (report values must match the controller's tracked last-activity) |
| Kubeflow Pipelines | Data Science Pipelines | Passive | Data source only — validated as an acceptance criterion on E002 (report values must match KFP run metadata) |

The strategy's premise is that both data sources already exist ("the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere"), and `.context/architecture-context/`
corroborates this (notebooks.md: last-activity tracking in the notebook
controller; data-science-pipelines.md: KFP v2 REST API with runs surfaced in the
Dashboard; dashboard.md: the Dashboard reads component CRs and owns no data
plane). Both passive components are validated by the same owning organization as
the consuming epic (console-side), so no separate validation epics are generated.

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9016-E001 idle-workbench report]
    E002[RHAISTRAT-9016-E002 stale pipeline-run report]
    E003[RHAISTRAT-9016-E003 documentation]
    E001 --> E003
    E002 --> E003
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 ∥ E002 (no edge) | Rule 15 | Same component and team, different areas: the idle-workbench report consumes Notebook CR / notebook-controller activity data while the stale-run report queries pipeline run metadata. No shared artifact; overlap is limited to console navigation placement, which is a merge-coordination risk, not a dependency. Splitting gives independently shippable reports and separately reviewable PRs. |
| E001 → E003 | Rule 11 | docs-authoring epic is blocked by ALL Implementation epics — documentation describes the reports that were actually built. |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 11 | Same — docs must follow both report implementations. |

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Epic | Notes |
|-----|------|-------|
| HLR-1 (P1) | E001 | Per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources) sourced from notebook-controller activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 (P1) | E002 | Stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts) sourced from KFP run metadata. |
| HLR-3 (P2) | E001 (bundled), E002 (bundled) | CSV export is a presentation mode of each report's own surface over the same data — it is not separately schedulable (splitting would build the same report surface twice), so each report epic implements the export for its own report. |
| HLR-4 (P2) | E003 | docs-authoring epic; priority derived from strategy frontmatter `priority: Normal` → P2 per the docs-authoring priority exception (no priority inheritance from implementations). |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

- **Missing strategy sections**: the strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
  Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no
  Non-Functional Requirements. Epic acceptance criteria were derived from the
  HLRs and problem statement. Owner teams were taken from the architecture
  context files (Dashboard → RHOAI Dashboard); the Documentation epic's owner
  ("RHAI Documentation") is assumed, as no team information exists for docs in
  the strategy or context.
- **Scope contingency (non-blocking)**: the strategy asserts the notebook
  controller's last-activity timestamps are already tracked and sourceable, and
  Open Questions is empty, so this is treated as an implementation detail of
  E001. However, notebooks.md describes activity tracking "per kernel through
  Jupyter server API probes" (the culler's mechanism); if the timestamp turns
  out not to be externally readable by the console, E001's sourcing approach
  changes and scope could expand into the Notebooks component. The epic carries
  a validation AC against the controller's tracked activity to surface this
  early.
- **Bundled lower-priority HLR**: HLR-3 (P2, CSV export) is bundled into both
  P1 report epics — see the traceability matrix row for the rationale.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — the strategy has no external dependencies with uncertain
timing; both report epics are independent and start immediately in parallel.
